title: Dynamic Proximity‑Weighted Routing and Safe Hosted Fallback Protocol
creator: Liam Patel
description: Implement a routing policy that weights region and tier selection by a proximity score (latency + network variance + historical tail) and introduces a controlled, observable hosted fallback protocol for Dedicated-to-Hosted spillover. The goal is to minimize customer-visible latency regressions when Dedicated capacity is exhausted while preventing uncontrolled quality regressions from fallback model variants.
acceptance_criteria: New proximity score computed per tenant per region and exposed in routing decision logs
When Dedicated capacity is unavailable, spillover chooses hosted variants according to priority clusters and variant-safety scores rather than naive shortest-path routing
Canary rollout: 1% of traffic uses new proximity weighting for 48h with no >5% increase in 99th percentile latency or >2% increase in quality regressions measured by prompt-set evals
Automatic rollback triggers on either latency SLO breach (p99 increased beyond configured delta) or quality regression above threshold
Audit logs include pre- and post-fallback model variant chosen, score breakdown (latency, capacity, variant-safety), and decision reason
technical_notes: Proximity score = 0.5 * normalized-network-latency + 0.3 * observed-p99-jitter + 0.2 * datacenter-health-penalty. Variant-safety score is computed from historical BLEU/ROUGE-like evals on tenant prompt-sets (KL-divergence on token distributions + hallucination signal). Routing decisions must be deterministic at the request bucket level to preserve tracing and replayability. Use the existing routing engine hook points; add a lightweight memory cache with TTL per tenant-region to avoid thundering updates.

Integration: wire module into capacity adjudicator with deterministic bucket hashing and add audit fields to request_trace — owner: infra — due 2026-03-15

rollout_plan: Stage 0 (internal): Feature flag off, unit/integration tests, local validation against synthetic traffic
Stage 1 (canary): Enable for 1% of production traffic for non‑SLA tenants with additional logging and shadowed outputs for quality evaluation (48h)
Stage 2 (broaden): Increase to 10% with tenants that opted into early routing changes; continue monitoring quality and latency metrics
Stage 3 (tiered): Enable for low‑priority Dedicated overflow paths only; keep high priority tenants on legacy routing until 7 days of stable metrics

Rollback criteria: immediate rollback if p99 latency for any impacted tenant increases >10% absolute or quality regression measured by tenant prompt-set exceeds configured threshold for 2 consecutive hours
testing_plan: Unit tests for proximity score normalization and deterministic hashing
Integration tests simulating Dedicated capacity exhaustion across regions with controlled network jitter
Shadow evaluation: run fallback variant outputs through the eval pipeline (existing eval infra) and compare KL/divergence and hallucination rate
Chaos test: introduce simulated region outage and verify spillover honors per-tenant quotas and does not route >5% of tenant requests to unknown model variants
Performance: microbench routing decision latency budget < 500 microseconds at p99 under 10k RPS
